title: Tilted plane (3+2): a Tool axis A of 180 degrees is refused with no reason, and the plane of the A0 B180 face has X and Y exchanged

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found during the work on #1904 ("Your first 4-axis part", Tormach 770MX + microARC 4), on `main` at `af83da0f4`.

A 4th-axis table about X can turn the part to A180. `tormach.cps` posts that index as `G0 A180`, and `the_canonical_b180_pose_posts_as_a180` pins it. But the operation page does not let the user ask for it directly.

## 1. A Tool axis A of 180 is refused, and the refusal gives no reason

Steps:
1. Mount `Tormach 770MX + microARC 4`. Add a tool and a box stock.
2. Add a Slot. On the Heights tab, tick **Tilted plane (3+2)**. Set **Tool axis A** to 180 and **Tool axis B** to 0. Choose **Apply**.

Result: the edit is refused with this text: `operation parameters are not usable for a Slot operation`. The MCP tool gives the same text: `add_operation: invalid parameters: operation parameters are not usable for a Slot operation`.

The cause is `Tilt::is_sane` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`. It accepts A from -90 to 90 and B from -180 to 180. The pose law writes the face opposite the top as A 0, B 180. The refusal does not name the tilt, the limits, or the A 0 B 180 pose. A microARC 4 user thinks in A only, and cannot find the remedy from this text.

The workaround is to type A 0 and B 180. The guide page for #1904 documents it.

## 2. The plane of the A 0 B 180 face has X and Y exchanged

`TiltedFrame::new` (`crates/cl/src/cl/frame.rs`) selects the in-plane axes from the smallest component of the tool axis. For A 90 and A -90, plane X is machine X (the rotary axis). For A 0 B 180, `sin(180 degrees)` is not exactly zero, the seed becomes Y, and plane X is machine Y and plane Y is machine X.

Result: the same flat along the bar has the ends (-0.75, 0) and (-0.25, 0) on three faces, but (0, -0.75) and (0, -0.25) on the fourth face. The page does not show the plane axes, so the user finds this only from the toolpath preview.

The posted program is correct in each case. The post reads the tool tip in machine coordinates.

## Proposed change

- Refuse an out-of-range tilt by name. Give the limits, and say that the face opposite the top is A 0 B 180.
- Or accept A beyond 90 degrees at the door and store the canonical pose.
- For a pose with no X component of the tool axis, keep plane X on machine X. Or show the plane X and Y directions on the page.

A change to the frame basis changes the paths of existing A 0 B 180 operations. Thus this work is under the safety floor.

Done means: a user who types Tool axis A = 180 on an A-table machine gets the A180 index or a refusal that names the remedy. The plane X of the A 0 B 180 face is on the rotary axis, or the page shows the plane axes. A test pins each item. The guide page `first-4axis-part.md` is updated.

Refs #1904, #797.
